Bottom rail is the return and carries the GND symbol.

CRITICAL SITE DECISIONS:
  S0 (513,382) deg=3 -> JUNCTION. The crop shows a clean T: the vertical column that feeds the inductor terminates on the horizontal top rail; there is no fourth branch above and no hop. A T can only be read as joined. Reading it as anything else would strand the inductor top on a one-terminal net and leave the 2k/5k midpoint floating.
  S13 (516,640) deg=4 -> JUNCTION. The inductor's bottom lead crosses the bottom rail and continues a short stub into the GND symbol; all four branches are drawn as a plain cross with no hop and no jog. Reading it as a crossing would put the GND stub and the inductor bottom on a net separate from the bottom rail, which would leave the V-AC bottom and the capacitor bottom with no ground reference and give the inductor no return path - electrically impossible. Junction is the only sane reading, and it is also what the ink prior says.
